subject: the wall-clock assertions in this test suite, and what they measure instead of the code
question: Can the property each timed assertion names be read off the implementation's own work count rather than off the clock?

host.note: Logic was NOT driven for this record. Every reading below comes from the test suite against FakeAXRuntimeBuilder, plus three CI runs. The block is generated by Scripts/observation_host.py because rule 5 forbids typing one, not because the host is what this is true of — what this is true of is the code.

reverify.expected: REVERIFY PASS: the bounded refusal stays under 20 censuses, the same refusal with no supplied timeout exceeds 40, both waitForSegmentVisible waits hold their counts, the traversal takes exactly 3101 probe calls, no test in Tests/ reads a clock, and the rule's 17 self-test cases pass
reverify.cost: no Logic and no live window; about 4 s of deliberate waiting inside a build

method: Three timed assertions were found by grepping Tests/ for clock reads. For each, the property its comment claimed was identified, a counter for the work the implementation actually repeats was added to the fixture, and the counted form was then mutation-tested: the defect the assertion exists to catch was injected into Sources/ and the test had to go red. The separation between the counted values was measured by deleting the argument under test rather than argued from the constants. The guard written afterwards was itself mutated three ways and its self-test had to catch each.

observations.note: three separate pull requests, none of which changed any Swift; the third was PR #807, whose only failing test in a 4433-test run was this one

observations.what: window structure censuses served by the fixture, with `confirmationTimeout: 0.025` passed
the same, with the argument deleted so the writer's 3 s `viewConfirmationTimeout` default applies
observations.note: 9.2x, and the run took 3.413 s against 0.404 s — the count moves with the property, the seconds move with the machine

observations.count: <= 4 as asserted; the wait returns on the first look
observations.mutation: the early `return` in waitForSegmentVisible replaced by a no-op
observations.note: burned the whole 1 s timeout, which is what the ceiling exists to refuse

observations.mutation: `rightmostColumnOnly` forced to false, so the left-column "Bass" is accepted
observations.note: the elapsed-time form it replaces needed 0.12 s of real waiting to say the same thing

observations.what: testEnumerateTree_Perf_100Folders_UnderBudget, probe calls for 100 folders x 30 presets
observations.note: exact, not a ceiling; the neighbouring T8 #20 already proves the 1 + 2n shape, so the elapsed < 2.0 s it replaces was adding only that the machine was fast. Run time fell from a 2 s budget to 0.008 s.

observations.what: the guard applied to the pre-fix file at origin/main

mutations: comment stripping removed — 3 cases go red
the Date().timeIntervalSince pattern deleted — 3 cases go red, including the verbatim line that failed CI
the .timeIntervalSinceNow pattern widened to match the constructor label — the fixed-instant case and the whole-repository case go red

observations.what: the counterfactual, as a checked-in control rather than a hand mutation
observations.note: a floor, because load takes a wait loop's count down and never up; it costs the ~3 s it bounds and is what makes the ceiling of 20 beside it a discriminating number rather than a decoration

conclusion: Every one of the three timed assertions in this suite was re-expressible as a count of work the implementation performs, and the counts separate the property from the machine: 13 against 119 censuses for the honoured timeout, and load can only push a wait loop's count DOWN, so the failure mode that reddened three unrelated pull requests is not reachable from the replacement. Two of the three got stronger in translation — the rightmost-column mutation is now caught in 0.001 s rather than needing 0.12 s of real waiting, and the traversal budget is an exact 3101 rather than a wall-clock ceiling.
limits: This says nothing about live Logic. Every reading is against FakeAXRuntimeBuilder; the 28-46 ms menu timing the original comment cited was measured elsewhere and is not re-measured here.

The 13-census figure is a reading of today's implementation, not a specification. A change to viewConfirmationPollInterval moves it, and the ceiling of 20 would then have to be re-derived rather than raised.
The guard reads text. A clock behind a helper of its own, mach_absolute_time, or a timing closure passed in would all pass it; what is closed is the spelling all three real instances used.
Sources/ is not scanned. Production code times things on purpose, and a rule that could not tell the two apart would be worse than none.
